dominant_breach: rising interest and primary-balance stress can crowd out floor protection while tax expenditures, asset supports, and backstops remain politically senior unless repair packages are incidence-scored
fastest_washout: debt-service pressure becomes a generalized austerity story while the cube fails to specify which claims are protected, which tax expenditures are spared, and who absorbs repair

public_balance_sheet_gate.note: Federal fiscal interest risk is an active public-balance-sheet gate: debt, interest, trust-fund promises, tax expenditures, credit programs, and backstops must be scored together rather than siloed.

public_debt_interest_crowdout.note: CBO and Treasury/GAO/IMF sources make interest-cost and fiscal-capacity pressure central to floor, enforcement, and public-investment durability.

debt_service_distributional_incidence.note: Aggregate debt-service projections are not enough; the case still needs distributional incidence across households, regions, cohorts, creditors, and protected tax expenditures.

primary_balance_sustainability.note: Primary-balance repair is politically and distributionally non-neutral; comfort is blocked without a repair pathway that protects ordinary claimants first.

public_backstop_seniority_waterfall.note: rev0319 adds claimant seniority waterfall; comfort depends on stress priority and residual payer visibility.

public_balance_sheet_register.exposure_name: Federal debt-service, claim-security, tax-expenditure, and repair-package incidence surface
public_balance_sheet_register.legal_authority: Federal budget process, Treasury borrowing authority, Social Security and Medicare statutes, credit-program accounting, tax-expenditure statutes, annual CBO/Treasury/GAO/IMF reporting
public_balance_sheet_register.claimant_perimeter: Beneficiaries, taxpayers, creditors, state/local governments, public employees, safety-net claimants, providers, asset holders, future cohorts
public_balance_sheet_register.maximum_exposure: Federal debt, projected interest costs, scheduled social-insurance claims, credit/guarantee backstops, tax expenditures, and contingent fiscal obligations across baseline and long-term horizons.
public_balance_sheet_register.expected_loss: Not a single credit loss; risk appears as interest crowdout, service cuts, tax increases, benefit/provider payment adjustments, tax-expenditure protection, or future debt rollover burden.
public_balance_sheet_register.stress_scenario: Higher-rate or recession stress raises net interest and deficits while trust-fund and health claims mature, forcing a repair package whose incidence is hidden or shifted to ordinary claimants.
public_balance_sheet_register.funding_source: Federal taxes, borrowing, spending reductions, benefit/provider changes, tax-expenditure reform, public-asset returns, and future budgets.
public_balance_sheet_register.loss_sharing: Repair must identify creditors/asset holders, tax-expenditure beneficiaries, high-income households, providers/intermediaries, current beneficiaries, workers, states, and future cohorts rather than using aggregate fiscal gap language.
public_balance_sheet_register.public_upside_recovery: Tax-expenditure rollback, enforcement recovery, progressive revenue, credit-pricing reform, public-asset return capture, and explicit backstop pricing before ordinary claimant haircut.
public_balance_sheet_register.ordinary_claimant_protection: Claimant floors, disability/survivor protections, care access, state/local essential services, and enforcement capacity must be senior to tax-expenditure preservation or asset-price support.
public_balance_sheet_register.sunset_or_review: Quarterly through 2026 while CBO, trustees, Treasury, and budget policy surfaces update; annual long-term outlook refresh thereafter.

seniority_waterfall.claimant: ordinary public claimants and essential services
seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Must be senior to aggregate austerity and opaque crowdout.
seniority_waterfall.notes: Interest is paid before many discretionary service choices become visible.

seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Claim security must be specified before solvency repair is certified.
seniority_waterfall.notes: Benefit formulas are law but financing stress can induce prospective cuts or tax changes.

seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Cannot remain politically senior by default without explicit incidence justification.
seniority_waterfall.notes: Infrastructure, enforcement, care supports, and local grants can absorb crowdout.

seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Cannot be the unpriced residual claimant for delayed repair.
seniority_waterfall.notes: Can pay through taxes, thinner services, delayed investment, or local fee/tax pressure.
